summary: The Rift Crown: the largest crown of the East after Noris, a court where both great roads end, with ferries to the Zilin Hills and a choice at the water.

court_of_alerhan_spirit.name: The Court of King Alerhan
court_of_alerhan_spirit.desc: Turquoise and ochre hangings fill the hall where Alerhan III hears his lords. Petitioners come from the dunes and the rift coast and leave with answers.

greatest_court.name: The Greatest Court of the East
greatest_court.desc: No hall in the East seats so many kings' envoys at once. The Rift Crown receives them all and keeps the greater share of every secret.

pilgrim_tolls.name: The Pilgrim Tolls
pilgrim_tolls.desc: Every pilgrim who sails for the hermitage pays a small coin at the quay. The coins are many, and the harbour masters have learned to count them quickly.

rift_sea_masters.name: Masters of the Rift Sea
rift_sea_masters.desc: Alerhia's steersmen know every current of the narrow sea and every shoal of both shores. Few crews dare to race them.

customs_of_alerhia_spirit.name: The Customs of Alerhia
customs_of_alerhia_spirit.desc: A written tariff hangs on every gate, and the toll-keepers answer to the king alone. Merchants grumble at the price and trust the count.

rift_ambition.name: The Rift Calls
rift_ambition.desc: The court has looked across the water and liked what it saw. Captains drill with a far shore in mind.

lord_of_far_shore.name: Lord of the Far Shore
lord_of_far_shore.desc: Alerhia holds towns on the elven coast, and its king sits among them as a lord among lords. The treasury has not yet learned to be modest about it.

open_ports.name: The Open Ports
open_ports.desc: Alerhia's quays stay open to every flag, and the harbour dues are fair and fixed. Ships from both shores prefer them to any other.

rift_crown_court.title: The Rift Crown
rift_crown_court.desc: Riders from Furvior and bankers from Postondoroth sit in the same antechamber, each pretending not to see the other. King Alerhan has not yet decided whom to receive first, and the whole court is watching his door.

roads_bid.title: The Roads Bid for Alerhia
roads_bid.desc: Each great road has named a price for Alerhia's friendship, and the king's treasurers have counted both twice. Whoever takes the gold takes also a rival, but the court can keep its freedom if it is careful with its promises.

focuses.name: The Rift Crown
focuses.desc: Alerhan's forebears took the narrow crown of rift pearls when the desert lords first agreed to follow one king. His court is rich, proud and courted from two roads at once.

focuses.name: The Court of King Alerhan
focuses.desc: The king sits under ochre and turquoise hangings and hears every petition in person. A court that listens learns who is lying.

focuses.name: Lords of the Desert Half
focuses.desc: The southern half of the realm is ruled by lords who rarely see the capital. The king sends them gifts, banners and tax-collectors, in that order, and they send back riders.

focuses.name: The King's Road Tax
focuses.desc: Both great roads end at Alerhia's gates, and everything that arrives pays. A fixed tariff and a counting-house on the Gold Road make the payment orderly.

focuses.name: The Mountain Marches
focuses.desc: The hills behind the capital hold narrow passes that no army has forced in living memory. The king mends their walls and posts a warden in each.

focuses.name: The Greatest Court of the East
focuses.desc: Envoys from every crown of the East now crowd Alerhia's hall, and the king receives them with the care of a man who knows he is watched. The Rift Crown is spoken of from Furvior to the southern sands.

focuses.name: The Pilgrim Ports
focuses.desc: Pilgrims by the thousand come to Alerhia's quays for the crossing to the hermitage. The harbour masters widen the moles and hang lanterns on every pier.

focuses.name: Ferries to Zilin
focuses.desc: Flat-bottomed ferries carry the faithful across the rift to the Deliverer's hermitage in the Zilin Hills. The temples on the waterfront grow rich on the traffic and generous with their thanks.

effects.tooltip: Pilgrims cross from our quays to the Deliverer's hermitage.

focuses.name: The Rift Fleet
focuses.desc: Oared galleys with shallow keels suit the narrow sea better than any deep-water hull. The yards on the east shore turn out a pair each season.

focuses.name: Traders of the Elder Groves
focuses.desc: Across the water the elves of the groves pay well for desert salt, dyed cloth and lamp wicks. A steady trade is the best argument for a lasting peace.

focuses.name: Harbour Forts of the Rift
focuses.desc: The moles are crowned with towers and chains, so that a hostile fleet must pass under the king's eye. Wardens learn every cry of the gulls and every mast on the horizon.

focuses.name: Master of the Rift Sea
focuses.desc: No ship crosses the narrow sea without Alerhia knowing of it. The king's admirals have charted both coasts and have begun to name the winds.

focuses.name: Where Two Roads End
focuses.desc: The Gold Road ends at the capital and the Rift Road at the harbours. Furvior's riders and Postondoroth's bankers each assume Alerhia is theirs; the king is not so sure.

effects.tooltip: Both great roads of the south end at our gates.

focuses.name: The Riders' Offer
focuses.desc: Furvior offers escorts for every caravan and a place at the riders' fires. The price is that the Rift Road should speak with Furvior's voice.

focuses.name: Let the Roads Bid
focuses.desc: The king sets two chairs in his hall and names no favourite. Each power may name its price, and Alerhia keeps its freedom for as long as the bidding lasts.

focuses.name: The Bankers' Offer
focuses.desc: Postondoroth offers credit, ledgers and a place at the counting-table. The loans are generous, and the books are long.

focuses.name: The Gold Road Gate
focuses.desc: A new gate of dressed stone closes the Gold Road at the capital. Caravans pass beneath its arch, and every wagon is marked and counted.

focuses.name: The Customs of Alerhia
focuses.desc: The tariff is written on bronze and fixed to the gate, so that no toll-keeper can raise it without the king knowing. Merchants trade where the rules are plain.

focuses.name: The Question of the Rift
focuses.desc: Envoys have begun to speak of rich, weak lands across the water, and of kings who rule them poorly. The court listens, and a map is unrolled on the long table.

focuses.name: Lord of the Crossing
focuses.desc: If the coalition forms, Alerhia will have the harbours, the steersmen and the heaviest court. A king who leads the crossing leads the whole venture.

focuses.name: Warden of the Rift
focuses.desc: The elves across the water have done Alerhia no harm, and their groves are older than the Rift Crown. A king who guards that shore guards his own name.

focuses.name: The Rift Crown Waits
focuses.desc: The king writes to neither side and sends the envoys home with gifts. A throne that waits is a throne that keeps its options.

focuses.name: Muster for the Crossing
focuses.desc: Banners gather at the quays and the lords of the dunes bring their riders to the water. The muster rolls are the longest the court has ever written.

focuses.name: The Crossing of the Rift
focuses.desc: The fleet sails at dawn with the host aboard, and the steersmen steer by the old stars. What lies on the far shore has been argued about for a year.

focuses.name: Lord of the Rift Shores
focuses.desc: Towns on the far coast now fly the Rift Crown's banner. The king rules them from the capital and learns how far a letter can travel in a season.

focuses.name: Aid the Elder Groves
focuses.desc: When the eastern host lands on the elven shore, Alerhia's warden-king sends word that he will stand with those it attacks. His treasury pays for the courage.

focuses.name: Keep the Ports Open
focuses.desc: Alerhia's quays take every flag and every cargo, and the harbour dues stay fixed through the worst of the news. A kingdom that stays open is a kingdom that stays rich.

focuses.name: Read the First Stair
focuses.desc: The first stair of Alerhia was raised above the flood-line so that the river and the gods would each have a place, and its lowest courses are older than the crown. The temple scribes go down into the vaults under it with lamps and wax tablets, and they come back talking of a bridge, a city cut in two and an old treaty with the elves.
